bullets.title: Advanced Assessment & Prioritisation in International Practice
bullets.text: International healthcare systems expect nurses to combine structured assessment tools with professional judgement. Adult patients may have multiple chronic illnesses, altered communication, polypharmacy and rapid changes in condition. Prioritisation must be based on risk, not convenience or routine.

bullets.title: Managing Complex Medical & Perioperative Care
bullets.text: Complex adult care requires nurses to anticipate complications, evaluate treatment response and coordinate multiple interventions. International practice emphasises evidence-based pathways, timely review and clear accountability.

bullets.title: Interdisciplinary Care, Documentation & Safe Transitions
bullets.text: Adult medical-surgical care is delivered by multidisciplinary teams. Nurses coordinate information across professions and shifts, making accurate documentation and handover essential to continuity and safety.

bullets.title: Person-Centred Education & Chronic Disease Self-Management
bullets.text: Many adults live with chronic conditions that require daily decisions after discharge. Education should build the patient's confidence and ability to recognise deterioration, use treatments correctly and seek help early.
